svg.title: Lens Calibration
svg.desc: How MagicFocus calibrates a lens. On the Calib. page you aim the lidar at a subject near 0.5, 2 or 4 m, focus it sharp with the arrows and press Save to SD, which stores the lidar reading and the motor position. Autofocus interpolates between the saved points in 1/distance: in an example lens with points 0.5 m at 1950, 2 m at 880 and 4 m at 700, the curve against distance bends, while against 1/distance it is straight between points. A reading of 1.0 m lies between the 0.5 m and 2 m points: t = (1/1.0 - 1/0.5) / (1/2 - 1/0.5) = 0.67, so the position is 1950 + 0.67 x (880 - 1950) = 1237; interpolating in metres would give 1593. Closer than the nearest or farther than the farthest saved point, the line through the two outermost points is extended, within the motor range of 0 to 4095, so the example reaches 4095 at about 0.2 m and 520 at infinity. A legend names the marks: saved points, the interpolated and the extrapolated position, and the example reading. Autofocus needs at least two points. The autofocus loop: lidar frames with strength of at least 100 and 10 to 1200 cm, a jump check that holds back jumps over 15 % until they last 30 ms, a median of the last 5 readings, hysteresis that ignores changes under 2 cm, the interpolation, a deadband that ignores changes under 24 counts, then a move along the chosen AF curve.
svg.text: Each saved point pairs a lidar distance with a motor position. Autofocus interpolates between them in 1/distance and extrapolates beyond them.
Calibrate: save two or three points per lens
Pick a point and aim the lidar
at a subject near 0.5, 2 or 4 m
with the arrows on the Calib. page
stores the actual reading and position
Interpolate and extrapolate: straight lines in 1/distance
Example lens with three saved points: 0.5 m → 1950, 2 m → 880, 4 m → 700.
Extrapolated beyond them, up to the motor’s end
For a reading d between two saved points (d₀, p₀) and (d₁, p₁):
Beyond the outermost points, the line through the two outermost is
extended, up to the motor's end. Autofocus needs two saved points.
Example: the lidar reads 1.0 m, between the 0.5 m and 2 m points
Interpolating in metres instead would give 1593.
Focus travel is close to linear in 1/distance, so these lines fit.
Autofocus loop: from a lidar reading to a motor move
Code: focusForDistance() in src/LensCalibration.h, the lidar filters in src/Lidar.h, updateAutofocus() in src/FocusControl.h.
